signals.title: Stop Parquet background reads before releasing the format's read buffer
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114612 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed heap memory corruption when reading Parquet through an input format that owns its read buffer, for example a dictionary with `SOURCE(FILE(... format 'Parquet'))`. Background prefetch and decode tasks could still read and write through the buffer after the pipeline released it, which could abort the server. ### Description Closes #114612, reported by @ PedroTadim, who asked me to go ahead in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114612#issuecomment-5278451991. A `ReadBuffer` handed to an input format via `addBuffer()` lives in the format's `owned_buffers`. `ISource::work()` calls `onFinish()` on both the clean and the exception path, reaching `IInputFormat::resetReadBuffer()`, which clears `owned_buffers` and destroys the buffer. `ParquetV3BlockInputFormat` did not override that hook, and `Parquet::Prefetcher` holds a non-owning `SeekableReadBuffer *` to the same buffer, so background tasks kept using a destroyed object. It is not only a bad read: the report on the issue is a 1 MiB **write** into freed heap through `ReadBuffer::next()`, silent on a release build. `~Prefetcher()` does the right handshake, but only at format destruction, later than `onFinish()`; that window is the bug. The fix overrides `resetReadBuffer()` to drain background tasks before the base class releases the buffers, mirroring `ParallelParsingInputFormat::onFinish()`. Three details are forced by the surrounding code: the hook is `resetReadBuffer()`, not `onFinish()`, since it frees the buffers and has a second caller in `StreamingFormatExecutor`; the reader is drained but kept alive, because `getMatchedBuckets()` reads row group metadata after exhaustion; and `ReadManager` is drained before `Prefetcher`, because decode tasks re-enter `readSync` inline via `getRangeData()`. Sibling teardown paths: `resetParser()` already destroys the reader before delegating, `onCancel()` cancels it, and the reuse route through `StreamingFormatExecutor` calls `resetParser()` on every exit, so a drained reader is never reused. No fuzzer needed: `ReadBufferFromFile` leaves `use_pread` false, so a local file takes `SeekAndRead`, and any `CREATE DICTIONARY ... SOURCE(FILE(... format 'Parquet'))` whose load throws reaches it. Validated on ASAN: the added test fails 7/7 unfixed, passes 11/11 fixed; a standalone reproducer 31/33 unfixed, 0/35 fixed; a negative control with only the override reverted reddens at the unfixed rate. Parquet and polygon-dictionary suites gave an identical failing set on both binaries (187 each); 50 randomized-settings repeats passed clean.

signals.title: Make the release job a linear step sequence without ok, recovery, or dry-run flags
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114472 --> Reworks `ci/jobs/release_job.py` into a linear sequence of steps. Per @maxknv, the release workflow should be linear, without checks in the orchestrator: the checks move into the steps, which are idempotent and self-gating. The orchestrator body no longer carries any `if ok` / recovery-flag / `dry-run` gating. What is left of each: - The `ok` short-circuit stays, but encapsulated in the `step()` helper: it skips the remaining steps once one fails, so callers no longer write `if ok and ...`. The always-run tail (`Checkout Back`, `Post`, `Clean Up Credentials`) still bypasses it so cleanup runs after a failure. - The recovery flags no longer gate the orchestrator. `is_recovery`, `is_late_recovery`, and the release-PR-state lookups (`release_pr_absent` / `release_pr_needs_merge`) are not read to decide which steps run. `release_info.json` is still read — for `release_tag` to build the changelog-generation step, and inside docker `build()` for the floating-tag flags — but never to gate step creation. - The `dry-run` gates move into the steps. Each step is invoked unconditionally and previews or skips its own mutations; the `create_release.py` steps already take `--dry-run`, and the inline `docker_login`, `verify_release_tools`, `setup_buildx`, and docker `build()` now guard their own mutations. Each affected check now lives in the step: - `push_release_tag` / `push_new_release_branch` self-skip when the tag / branch already exists, so a recovery is a no-op — this answers the review that an idempotent operation should not need an `is_recovery` gate. - The changelog-PR step moves out of `release_job.py` into `create_release.py` (`--create-changelog-pr`), so like every other step it is a `create_release.py` invocation whose checks live in the step: rerun-safe (existing-PR lookup, "already up to date" skip) and skips when its PR is already merged, replacing the old `release_pr_absent` gate. The version-bump step is likewise rerun-safe without that gate. - The docker floating-tag decision reads `is_late_recovery` / `latest` from the step's own release info rather than from orchestrator closure variables. - The skip-repo/skip-docker-must-be-a-recovery check moves into `prepare`, which is passed `--skip-repo` / `--skip-docker` and refuses a non-recovery ref there. What remains in the orchestrator body is only workflow-input gating (release type, `skip-repo` / `skip-docker`) — the mode selectors that decide which steps exist at all. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):

signals.title: Do not hold the DDL guard during TRUNCATE
signals.text: `TRUNCATE TABLE` held the table's DDL guard while removing data, and truncate can wait for running merges or for other replicas to process `DROP_RANGE`. Any DDL on that name — including background threads that need it — was blocked for that whole time. Release the guard before `IStorage::truncate` for databases with UUIDs, matching `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION`, which never took it. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `TRUNCATE TABLE` no longer blocks concurrent `DROP`, `RENAME` and other DDL queries on the same table while the data is being removed.

signals.title: Read a subcolumn of an `ALIAS` parent through a `Merge` table instead of a default
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112975 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix reading a subcolumn (`.size0`, `.null`, a tuple element, `String.size`) through a `Merge` table when the underlying table declares the parent column as `ALIAS`. Such a read returned the type default, and when the parent was selected in the same query it could return the value of an unrelated column. ### Description Selecting `arr.size0` from a `Merge` table returns `0` when the child declares `arr` as an `ALIAS` column, while the same query against the child returns the correct `5`: ```sql CREATE TABLE ag (n UInt64, arr Array(UInt8) ALIAS [1,2,3,4,5]) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO ag (n) VALUES (77); CREATE TABLE mg (arr Array(UInt8), n UInt64) ENGINE = Merge(currentDatabase(), '^ag$'); SELECT arr.size0 FROM mg; -- 0, should be 5 ``` Root cause: `ColumnsDescription::add` registers no subcolumns for an `ALIAS` column, because the value has to be extracted after the expression is evaluated. So `arr.size0` does not resolve against the child, but does against the `Merge` table, where `arr` is ordinary. `ReadFromMerge::getModifiedQueryInfo` reads that as "the child does not have this column": it substitutes a constant default, and its `with_aliases` loop skips the column, so the child is never asked for the data. With the parent also selected, alias expansion put the alias's dependency column in the child read list, and the misaligned read surfaced that value under the subcolumn's name. The analyzer already implements the extract-after-evaluation contract, turning such a name into `getSubcolumn` over the alias expression. This teaches both guards to recognise the case and route it to the existing alias branch with the full identifier, adding no new carrier. Also wrong for `Tuple.a`, `String.size` and `Nullable.null` (a NULL read back as non-NULL), under `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` 0 and 1, and it mis-scoped a row policy. `Map` subcolumns raise `NO_SUCH_COLUMN_IN_TABLE` before and after. The old analyzer raises `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` and is unchanged, hence the `no-old-analyzer` tag. `MATERIALIZED` and `DEFAULT` parents were already correct, and the default substitution for a child genuinely lacking a column is preserved; both have test arms. A mistyped child (`String ALIAS` under an `Array(UInt8)` Merge column) stays as it is, because `String` has no `size0`. That conversion case is #112975.

signals.title: Fix ANY/SEMI RIGHT JOIN with OR conditions emitting rows twice or losing matches
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112640 `ANY RIGHT JOIN` and `SEMI RIGHT JOIN` emit every row of their right table at most once, and exactly once when the row has a match. With several OR-ed conditions in `ON` the claim for that was taken with a single CAS on the head row of the matched key's `RowRefList`, while `addFoundRowAll` then emitted every row of that list and discarded the result of the per-row `setUsedOnce` it called afterwards. With `OR` a right row is reachable through several keys in several hash maps, so a per-key claim does not partition the right rows: a list whose head row was claimed through another condition was skipped whole, orphaning its other rows, and a list whose head row was still free re-emitted rows another left row had already taken. Some right rows then appeared twice and others lost their match — padded with defaults for `ANY RIGHT JOIN`, dropped entirely for `SEMI RIGHT JOIN` — varying from run to run with the probe order under `max_threads > 1`. The claim is now taken per emitted row: `addFoundRowAll` claims a row before appending it and skips the rows whose CAS it loses, and returns whether it appended anything so the left row is filtered in only then. A single disjunct keeps the per-key claim, which is exact there, since one key owns all of its rows. The residual-condition path (`joinRightColumnsWithAdditionalFilter`) already claimed per row and is unchanged. Besides writing `ANY RIGHT JOIN` / `SEMI RIGHT JOIN` directly, this is reached by a plain `ANY LEFT JOIN` whenever the planner swaps the tables (`query_plan_join_swap_table`, `auto` by default), which is how the issue was reported. Measured on the reported query before and after, at `max_threads = 8`: 20 of 60 runs returned 5 or 6 rows for a 4-row left table, now 60/60 return 4. On a 1000-row shape, `SEMI RIGHT JOIN` returned 200 rows instead of 1000; `ANY LEFT JOIN` padded 416–736 rows with defaults although they had a match, and with `max_joined_block_size_rows = 7` also returned 1008 rows for 1000 left rows. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ANY RIGHT JOIN` and `SEMI RIGHT JOIN` with several `OR`-ed conditions in the `ON` section returning some rows of the right table twice and losing the matches of others. A written `ANY LEFT JOIN` was affected too, because the planner may swap the tables and execute it as `ANY RIGHT JOIN`.
signals.author: vdimir

signals.title: Add a DISTINCT regression test for Merge over Distributed
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112931 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Test only. Related: #112931, already merged, which carries the fix. #112931 stopped `ReadFromMerge` from narrowing the per-shard-sorted streams of a `Distributed` child. Its tests (`04666`, `04813`) assert the resulting row order. The same concatenation also produced a wrong result *multiset* under `DISTINCT` - `DistinctSortedStreamTransform` removes only adjacent duplicates, so the second shard's sorted run survived and every value came back twice - and an order assertion cannot express that. @ zlareb1 reported this manifestation on #111211. The aggregating queries cover the stage above `WithMergeableState`, where the sort is merge-only because the shards already aggregated and sorted. `04813` asserts a pipeline shape for that stage, not a result. Both directions, default settings apart from `max_threads`, on the pre-fix release binary `26.7.4.27` (its `should_not_narrow` lacks the guard) and on master `068ec6d2ae62` (which has it): | Queries | pre-fix | master | |---|---|---| | `DISTINCT` / `DISTINCT ON` over the `Merge` table | 42 | 21 | | `GROUP BY ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT 3` over the `Merge` table | 9 8 7 | 9 9 8 | | the same `DISTINCT` straight through the `Distributed` table (control) | 21 | 21 | 50 of 50 runs pass under `clickhouse-test` with setting randomization on, and corrupting any asserted line to its pre-fix value fails the test. `optimize_distinct_in_order = 1` and `max_threads = 1` are pinned because the runner randomizes them and either one hides the bug. The row count comes from a subquery carrying the `LIMIT`: a bare `SELECT count()` lets the optimizer drop the `ORDER BY` and returns 21 even before the fix. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111211
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Precompute hashes and prefetch for fixed-size-keys aggregation methods
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114638 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104475 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/81944 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): For the `keys32`/`keys64`/`keys128`/`keys256` family of aggregation methods (several fixed-size keys packed into one integer), precompute the per-row canonical hashes in one pass over the batch-packed keys and reuse them to software-prefetch the target bucket and to skip rehashing the key in `emplace`. Previously the look-ahead prefetch computed every key and its hash twice per row. --- This extends the precomputed-hash + prefetch mechanism that #104475 introduced for the `prealloc_serialized` family to `HashMethodKeysFixed` (multi-key `GROUP BY` over numeric columns, e.g. ClickBench Q30/Q31/Q32). When the whole block of keys is batch-packed upfront (`prepared_keys`), the per-row canonical hashes are computed in one pass on the first `emplace`/`find` call and reused both for the look-ahead prefetch and for the insert itself, replacing the generic look-ahead in `Aggregator::executeImplBatch` that builds every key holder and hashes it a second time per row. Details: - The runtime gates mirror `prealloc_serialized`: batch-packed keys available, `enable_software_prefetch_in_aggregation`, and the `min_bytes_for_prefetch` hash-table size threshold (checked lazily on the first call, when `Data` is known). Nullable and low-cardinality variants never use `prepared_keys` and are excluded at compile time. - A new concept `HasPrefetchByHashMemberFunc` compiles the path out for tables without hash-addressed buckets (`FixedHashTable` behind `keys16`). Set, JOIN and `arrayUniq`-style callers of `HashMethodKeysFixed` pass no settings context, so nothing changes for them. - `HashMethodSerializedContext` carried only the settings and is now the shared `HashMethodSettingsContext`, also used by `HashMethodKeysFixed::createContext`. - `HashTable::isEmptyCell` (the `findKey` short-circuit for precomputed hashes, used in the `no_more_keys` mode) is made zero-key-aware: the zero key is stored outside the buffer, so an empty cell at the key's place proves nothing when the zero key is present. The existing user (`prealloc_serialized`) never produces empty keys, so this was latent; an all-zeros fixed key is common (the ClickBench `hits` table has a `SearchEngineID = 0, ClientIP = 0` group). Correctness was verified against an unpatched build of the same commit on the full ClickBench `hits` dataset (identical single part, 99,997,497 rows): full-result checksums for `keys32`/`keys64`/`keys128`/`keys256`, nullable keys and `prealloc_serialized`; the all-zero key group; the `no_more_keys` path (`max_rows_to_group_by` with `group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'`); and external aggregation (spill + merge). All results are identical. An honest note on measured impact, from the investigation written up in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114638#issuecomment-5285053418: in a local interleaved A/B on a (noisy, shared) 96-core aarch64 box, this change measures neutral on ClickBench Q30/Q31/Q35 — the generic look-ahead prefetch already covered these methods, so the remaining saving is one packed-key load plus one CRC per row. The issue's local reproduction numbers for these queries turned out to be dominated by an unrelated effect (the memory-based `max_threads` cap from #100383, which the pre-#100383 baseline build does not have — details in the issue). The perf tests that exercise these exact shapes (`tests/performance/clickbench.xml` Q30/Q31/Q32, `group_by_fixed_keys.xml`, `hash_table_sizes_stats.xml`) should be the arbiter on dedicated hardware.

signals.title: Support aggregate functions in the trivial GROUP BY LIMIT optimization
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114637 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/81944 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114695 The trivial `GROUP BY ... LIMIT n` optimization (`optimize_trivial_group_by_limit_query`, default `true`) now also fires for projections **with aggregate functions**, e.g. ClickBench Q17 (`SELECT UserID, SearchPhrase, COUNT(*) FROM hits GROUP BY UserID, SearchPhrase LIMIT 10`), while keeping the aggregate values of the returned keys **exact**. **Why it was restricted.** The settings-based rewrite (`max_rows_to_group_by = n + offset` with `group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'`) enforces the cutoff per aggregation stream: a key kept by one stream and rejected by another loses the other stream's rows and comes out of the merge with an undercounted value. Returning an unspecified subset of the groups is fine for `LIMIT` without `ORDER BY`; returning wrong values is not. **How it works now (shared kept keys, zero hot-path cost).** The streams aggregate completely normally until the first one exceeds `n + offset` distinct keys (the pre-existing per-block `checkLimits`). That stream publishes a frozen seed of exactly `n + offset` kept keys with empty aggregate states (`ManyAggregatedData::SharedKeptKeys`); every stream then rebuilds its hash table to exactly that key set — keeping the states it accumulated for the kept keys, dropping the rest — and continues on the pre-existing `no_more_keys` path against a table of `n + offset` keys. Streams that finished consuming before the freeze are rebuilt by the last stream before the merge. Every row before the freeze is aggregated normally and every later row of a kept key finds its key in the rebuilt table, so the merged values are exact; the dropped keys are absent from every rebuilt table and never reach the result. The rebuild reuses the existing two-stage machinery (`convertToChunks(final = false)` + `mergeOnBlock`), so the hot aggregation loops in `Aggregator.cpp` are untouched. **Where it fires.** The cutoff is detected in the planner and enabled only when the node performs the complete aggregation itself (first and second stage): partial states sent to a remote initiator would be merged with other nodes' states, whose kept keys differ, and the values would be undercounted again — across nodes instead of across threads. On the shards of distributed queries and on the replicas of parallel-replicas reading it stays off. The settings-based rewrite of `OptimizeTrivialGroupByLimitPass` remains for aggregate-free projections (it is sound cross-shard). For the 8/16-bit key methods (fixed hash maps bounded by the key space) the cutoff stays inert and the aggregation is complete and exact. External aggregation is disabled when the cutoff is armed (spilled buckets would bypass the restriction); memory stays bounded by roughly `n + offset` keys plus one block of keys per stream. **Guards for wrong results of the existing optimization.** The shape check (shared between the pass and the planner, `getTrivialGroupByLimit`) now also rejects `DISTINCT`, `QUALIFY`, window functions and `arrayJoin` in the projection. These consume or filter the groups after the aggregation, and all four cases were verified to return wrong results on master with the default settings (e.g. `SELECT DISTINCT intDiv(k, 25000) FROM t GROUP BY k LIMIT 3` returned 1 row instead of 3; `SELECT count() OVER () FROM t GROUP BY k LIMIT 5` returned ~100 instead of 100000). Test `04837` pins all four in both the top-level (pass) and subquery (planner) forms. The guards are also submitted separately as the minimal backportable bug fix https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114695 (issue https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114693); whichever merges second needs a trivial conflict resolution. **Measured** on a 96-core aarch64 box, `SELECT number % 100000000 AS k, count() FROM numbers_mt(200000000) GROUP BY k LIMIT 10`: 0.06–0.13 s with the optimization vs 0.37–0.94 s without (interleaved hot runs on a shared machine). The values of the returned keys match the full aggregation exactly (verified by the `04836` join-against-truth tests for `UInt64`/`String`/`LowCardinality`/`Nullable`/two-key shapes, `count`/`sum`/`min`/`max`/`uniqExact`, with `OFFSET`, under single-stream and 16-stream execution, from aggregate projections, and over `remote()`). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The trivial `GROUP BY ... LIMIT n` optimization (setting `optimize_trivial_group_by_limit_query`) now also applies to queries with aggregate functions in the projection, such as ClickBench Q17: once any aggregation thread exceeds `n + offset` distinct keys, all threads are restricted to a single shared set of kept keys, so the hash tables stay small while the aggregate values of the returned keys remain exact (about 2x on ClickBench Q17). Additionally, the optimization no longer fires for queries with `DISTINCT`, `QUALIFY`, window functions, or `arrayJoin` in the projection, where it could return wrong results. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Parallelize single-level to two-level conversion in Aggregator::prepareVariantsToMerge
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114640 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107490 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickBench/pull/1360 When some per-thread aggregation states convert themselves to two-level mid-scan, `Aggregator::prepareVariantsToMerge` converts all the remaining single-level variants **sequentially on one thread**. Initializing a two-level variant allocates and zeroes 256 bucket tables, and there is one variant per query thread, so on machines with many cores this serial loop dominates short aggregation queries. This regime became reachable after #107490: the accurate aggregation memory accounting makes `group_by_two_level_threshold_bytes` (default 50 MB) engage for queries with **few groups but heavy states** (e.g. `uniqExact` over ~300 groups, where the states sum to hundreds of MB while the hash tables stay tiny). Previously the query-tracker delta under-reported such memory (each thread batches up to `max_untracked_memory` before propagating), so the threshold effectively never fired for this shape. Once it fires mid-scan, only the variants that happen to execute a block after the crossing convert themselves (measured: ~25 of 192 on ClickBench Q11), and the merge preparation then serially converts the remaining ~170. Effect on ClickBench (`c7a.metal-48xl`, 192 cores), hot runs, bisected and measured via manual ClickBench dispatches (evidence and result files in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickBench/pull/1360): | build | Q10 | Q11 | |---|---|---| | master `c79b0d9227e` (4 min before #107490) | 0.133 | 0.092 | | master `32129f76fca` (4 min after #107490) | 0.297 | 0.165 | | master 07-11 (`ab8535b3ab0`) | 0.391 | 0.213 | | master 07-11 + `group_by_two_level_threshold_bytes=0` | 0.093 | 0.102 | | pre-#107490 + `group_by_two_level_threshold=1` (uniform early conversion) | 0.132 | 0.095 | The last two rows show the cost is specifically the serial merge-prep conversion after a mid-scan flip: disabling the bytes trigger recovers fully, and uniform early conversion (which happens in parallel, each thread converting its own variant during the scan) is also fast. The daily ClickBench dashboard shows the same regression on both `c7a.metal-48xl` and `c8g.metal-48xl` (192 physical cores) since 2026-07-19, and not on machines with 96 or fewer physical cores. The fix converts the remaining single-level variants in parallel on the aggregator thread pool, following the existing `ThreadPoolCallbackRunnerLocal` pattern used elsewhere in the file. Converting distinct variants concurrently is safe: `AggregatedDataVariants::convertToTwoLevel` touches only the variant's own members. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Parallelize the single-level to two-level conversion of per-thread aggregation states before merging. This fixes a 2-3x regression of short `GROUP BY` queries with heavy aggregate states (e.g. `COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`, ClickBench Q10/Q11) on machines with very many cores, introduced in 26.7 development builds when the aggregation memory accounting was made accurate. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Fix wrong results of the trivial GROUP BY LIMIT optimization with DISTINCT, QUALIFY, window functions or arrayJoin
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114693 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114690 The trivial `GROUP BY ... LIMIT` optimization (`optimize_trivial_group_by_limit_query`, default `true` since 26.5) caps the aggregation at `LIMIT + OFFSET` distinct keys, which is only sound when the LIMIT directly cuts the produced groups. The shape check missed four constructs that consume or filter the groups **between** the aggregation and the LIMIT, and each of them returned wrong results with default settings (verified on master; reproducers in the issue and in the added test): - `DISTINCT` collapses the projected groups: `SELECT DISTINCT intDiv(k, 25000) FROM t GROUP BY k LIMIT 3` returned **1 row instead of 3**. - A window function in the projection is evaluated over all groups (`hasWindow` only catches the named `WINDOW` clause, not an inline `OVER ()`): `SELECT count() OVER () FROM t GROUP BY k LIMIT 5` returned **~100 instead of 100000**. - `arrayJoin` in the projection can drop rows (empty arrays), so the kept groups may produce fewer rows than the LIMIT while more groups exist: **1 row instead of 10**. - `QUALIFY` filters the groups after the aggregation: **0 rows instead of 10** (a `QUALIFY` on plain group keys alone is pushed down below the aggregation and was not affected; a window function in the projection keeps it in place). The pass now skips these shapes. https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114690 contains the same guards as part of a shared shape-check helper; whichever merges second needs a trivial conflict resolution, and this separate pull request keeps the wrong-results fix minimal and backportable on its own. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results of the trivial `GROUP BY ... LIMIT` optimization (setting `optimize_trivial_group_by_limit_query`) for queries with `DISTINCT`, `QUALIFY`, window functions, or `arrayJoin` in the projection: these consume or filter the groups after the aggregation, so capping the aggregation at `LIMIT + OFFSET` keys could return too few rows or wrong values. The optimization no longer applies to such queries. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Persist allow_archive_path_syntax in storage metadata
signals.text: Persistent storage definitions currently re-read `allow_archive_path_syntax` whenever their metadata is parsed. As a result, a path containing `::` can change between a literal path and archive syntax after `DETACH`/`ATTACH` or a server restart. This change resolves the setting when a persistent definition is created, stores it in metadata, and reuses the stored value during reload. Pre-existing metadata without the marker deterministically retains the historical archive-enabled interpretation. The fix covers `File`, `URL`, object-storage engines, `S3Queue`, and catalog-backed data-lake databases, with regression coverage for reloads and cold restarts. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114491 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/91062 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes persisted `File`, `URL`, `S3`, `S3Queue`, and catalog-backed data-lake definitions changing the meaning of paths containing `::` after `DETACH`/`ATTACH` or a server restart. The creation-time value of `allow_archive_path_syntax` is now stored in metadata and reused whenever the definition is loaded.

signals.title: Support PromQL histogram_fraction for classic histograms
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL: support `histogram_fraction()` for classic histograms. ### Description **What was missing** Prometheus supports `histogram_fraction(lower, upper, b)` for estimating the fraction of observations between two bounds. ClickHouse previously rejected this function in TimeSeries PromQL queries. **What this PR adds** - Adds support for classic Prometheus bucket series. - Reuses the existing classic histogram handling used by `histogram_quantile`. - Matches Prometheus behavior for interpolation and bucket edge cases. - Keeps different histogram metric names separate during aggregation. - Removes the input metric name from the result. Example: ```promql histogram_fraction(0.1, 0.5, http_request_duration_seconds_bucket) ``` ### Why this matters **This is used for real latency and SLO queries**, not only parser compatibility. - **Pyrra:** generates `histogram_fraction()` in native-histogram latency SLO rules. See the [query generator](https://github.com/pyrra-dev/pyrra/blob/main/slo/promql.go#L761-L784) and [example SLO config](https://github.com/pyrra-dev/pyrra/blob/main/examples/pyrra-connect-latency.yaml#L14-L20). - **Grafana SLO:** uses it in a [request-latency SLI query](https://grafana.com/docs/plugins/grafana-slo-app/latest/sli-examples/latency/). - **Grafana Mimir:** documents it for calculating the [fraction of requests in a latency range](https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/visualize/native-histograms/). - **Prometheus:** uses it for [fraction and Apdex calculations](https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/histograms/). Without this function, PromQL copied from these workflows fails in ClickHouse. ### Scope - **Supported:** classic `*_bucket` histogram series. - **Supported:** constant scalar lower and upper bounds. - **Not supported yet:** native histogram samples. - **Not supported yet:** non-constant bound expressions. Native histogram samples are not supported by the current TimeSeries Engine. This PR intentionally covers the classic bucket form first. ### References - [Prometheus histogram functions](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/functions/#histogram_fraction) - [Prometheus classic histogram implementation](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/promql/quantile.go) ### Changes - **Function support:** add `histogram_fraction` to the TimeSeries function registry and support documentation. - **Execution:** add a Prometheus-compatible classic histogram fraction aggregate. - **Shared logic:** reuse the histogram SQL-building pipeline with `histogram_quantile`. - **Precision:** preserve Float64 bound literals for Float32 tables and exact cumulative-count differences for large UInt64 counts. ### Tests - **Interpolation:** normal buckets, `rate()` input, negative bucket bounds, and bounds inside buckets. - **Bucket edges:** exact boundaries, degenerate buckets, `+Inf`, `NaN`, malformed `le`, and out-of-range bounds. - **Grouping:** range queries with multiple histogram groups and `sum by (le)` aggregation. - **Input validation:** invalid argument types and non-constant bounds. - **Float32:** regression coverage for precision near an `le` boundary. - **UInt64:** regression coverage for one-count differences above `2^53`. - **Compliance:** add classic histogram fraction queries to the PromQL compliance cases. - **Checks:** `git diff --check` and Python syntax validation for the integration test files.

signals.title: Do not prune with an invalid polygon in pointInPolygon key analysis
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114630 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed rows missing from the result of a `SELECT` filtered by `pointInPolygon` over a MergeTree primary key when the polygon argument is an invalid constant literal and `validate_polygons = 0`. Primary key analysis derived granule pruning from a polygon it never validated, and dropped granules holding matching rows. Closes: #114630 ### Description Primary key analysis of `pointInPolygon` built its filter from a constant ring that was never checked with `boost::geometry::is_valid`, unlike `parseConstPolygon` and the GeoParquet pruning path. `bg::correct` does not repair a self-intersection, so the unusable ring reached `bg::intersects`, whose relate-based answer disagrees with the grid algorithm the function itself evaluates. Granules holding matching rows were pruned away. Under the default `validate_polygons = 1` the function rejects the ring while folding the constant, before part selection, so this is only reachable with `validate_polygons = 0`. On the reporter's reproducer: 849 rows against 875 for the same data with a key that permits no such atom, 26 rows lost, 0 spurious. The fix validates the ring and declines the atom when it is invalid, so no pruning happens and the full scan returns the correct rows. This mirrors `GeoBbox.h`, which refuses to produce a pruning bbox rather than throwing; index analysis must not raise user errors. The check is deliberately not gated on `validate_polygons`: with validation enabled the query already fails earlier, so gating it there would keep the bug for exactly the users who can reach it. One correction to the issue text: both argument forms are affected, since they reach the same analysis lambda. The reporter's own three-argument case (794 against 820) shows it. Every polygon in the existing primary key and minmax pruning tests is valid, so their pruning is unchanged: a valid ring still reports the same `Granules: 289/1250`. signals.title: Check PREWHERE column support inside lambda bodies
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114206 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a logical error and a `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` error when a `PREWHERE` expression reads a table column inside a lambda body, e.g. `PREWHERE arrayMap(x -> t.c, [1])[1] > 0`. Such a column was never checked against the table expression's supported `PREWHERE` columns, so a `Merge` whose children declare it with different types built the filter against the wrong one rather than refusing it. Also fixes `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION` for a `PREWHERE` expression calling an executable or WebAssembly UDF that does not itself read a `JOIN` column. ### Description `CollectPrewhereTableExpressionVisitor::needChildVisit` skipped `LAMBDA`, so a column read only inside a lambda body never reached `visitImpl`, the one place that picks the table expression `PREWHERE` reads from and enforces `supportedPrewhereColumns`. On master: - A `Merge` whose children declare `x` as `UInt32` and `Nullable(UInt32)` excludes `x` from its contract, but the guard that would refuse it never runs. The filter is built against the root's type while a child reads another, so the lambda's `ColumnFunction` capture fails in the reader: `Cannot capture column N ... incompatible type`, a logical error, so an abort under sanitizers. - With no column visited, `PREWHERE` is pinned to the first table expression, so a lambda over another fails `Code: 10` (#114206). The fix descends into lambda bodies, skipping only the lambda's own parameters by testing for a `LAMBDA_ARGS` column source, as the sibling `CollectSourceColumnsVisitor` already does: a node type, not a function name, so all higher-order functions are covered. Collecting those columns makes two latent omissions live. `ReplaceColumnsVisitor` never entered a lambda either, so the `JOIN` type substitution that `PREWHERE` must roll back survived inside a lambda and aborted at `join_use_nulls = 1`. Rolling it back also re-derives the lambda's parameter types from the array its higher-order function iterates. It also rebuilt every function in the expression, replaced or not, through `FunctionFactory`, which does not own UDFs: hence the `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION`. It is now bounded to replaced subtrees, so a UDF reading a restored `JOIN` column stays refused as on master. Reported by @ nikitamikhaylov on [#113768](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113768#issuecomment-5268962866): one `Server died` in that PR's unrelated Stress test (amd_msan), [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113768&sha=8f8aef10f381104c26153d7fb829b7e196825b0b&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress+test+%28amd_msan%29). <details><summary>Validation</summary> Reproducer (aborts on master, `ILLEGAL_PREWHERE` with this change): ```sql CREATE TABLE t (x UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); CREATE TABLE t2 (x Nullable(UInt32)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t VALUES (100); INSERT INTO t2 VALUES (300); SET enable_analyzer = 1; SELECT x FROM merge(currentDatabase(), '^t') AS m PREWHERE (arrayMap(x -> m.x, [1])[1]) > 50; ``` `04879_prewhere_lambda_body_column_check`: 29 arms A/B'd against a base build, 8 refusals and 21 row-returning. Every refusal and every `join_use_nulls` shape is paired with the same query without a lambda, so each expected outcome is justified against master's own answer. | arm | base | with this change | |---|---|---| | diverging child types, lambda reads `m.x` (also `*`, `arrayFilter`) | abort | `ILLEGAL_PREWHERE` | | `ARRAY JOIN`ed alias inside a lambda | `Code: 10` | `ILLEGAL_PREWHERE` | | lambda over the second table of a `JOIN` | `Code: 10` | resolves to that table | | `LEFT JOIN`, right column in `arrayExists`, `join_use_nulls` 0 and 1 (#114206) | abort or `Code: 10` | `1` / `2` | | the same four without a lambda | as after the change | unchanged | | agreeing types; `WHERE`; unrestricted table; shadowed parameter | rows | unchanged | `04889_prewhere_lambda_executable_udf` covers the UDF case in 9 arms, with a built-in control. Five mutation arms, disjoint casualties: reverting `needChildVisit` re-introduces the abort and the `Code: 10`; dropping the `LAMBDA_ARGS` guard breaks `04108`; reverting `ReplaceColumnsVisitor` aborts in `ActionsDAG`; dropping either return-type refresh or the parameter-type re-derivation aborts in planning or in `ColumnFunction::appendArgument`. `04108`, `03036_prewhere_lambda_function`, `00729_prewhere_array_join` and `02955_analyzer_using_functional_args` pass unchanged. Both new tests ran 50x, 0 failures: `04879` under randomized settings, `04889` at `clickhouse-local` defaults. </details>

signals.title: Show file sizes next to artifact links in CI reports
signals.text: Praktika reports link to files — build artifacts, job logs, uploaded reports — without saying how large they are. A link to `clickhouse-common-static_26.8.1.1332_amd64.deb` gives no hint whether it is 300 KiB or 1.2 GiB, which matters when deciding what to download from a report such as https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=1bfa2815c410fb75b3fe6cfa4ef7877d82b63ea6&name_0=MasterCI Now every link to an uploaded file shows its size: `clickhouse-common-static_26.8.1.1332_amd64.deb (1.2 GiB)`, in both places file links appear — the widget on a job page and the expanded info row of any result. The size cannot be fetched by the report page itself: it is served from `s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports`, build artifacts live on `clickhouse-builds.s3.amazonaws.com`, and neither bucket sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so a cross-origin `HEAD` request is blocked by the browser. Instead the size is recorded at upload time: `copy_file_to_s3` remembers the size of every object it uploads, and `Result` stores it in `ext["link_sizes"]` as a `{link: bytes}` map for `json.html` to render. This costs about 0.3% of a gzipped report. Links with no recorded size — a link to another report, or any report produced before this change — render exactly as before. `json.html` has to be deployed for existing report URLs to pick up the rendering change. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1383` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: CI: run the full test suite only when review threads are resolved
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114724 While a PR has unresolved review threads, running the full test suite is a waste: the code is expected to change again once the review comments are addressed. This PR implements the gate requested in the issue: - A new `review_threads.py` pre-hook in the `Config Workflow` counts the PR's unresolved review threads (via GraphQL `reviewThreads`) and stores the state in the workflow kv data. While threads are unresolved, `should_skip_job` runs only builds and the preliminary checks (`Style check`, `Fast test`), plus the `Code Review` job — the AI review keeps re-checking pushed code and resolves its own addressed threads, which is what re-triggers the full suite automatically. - The `can_be_merged.py` post-hook re-checks the live thread state at finish time and turns the `Mergeable Check` red while threads are unresolved, or while only the limited pipeline ran (even if the threads were resolved mid-run — the full suite still has not run). The per-run verdict is recorded in a new `Review Threads` commit status, which doubles as immediate feedback on the PR. This also makes the decision on the AI review's comments once they are ready, as suggested in the issue: comments posted during the run are seen by the finish-time check. - A new `Rerun On Review Threads` workflow detects state changes and re-runs the last completed `PR` workflow run for the current head commit whenever the recorded verdict disagrees with the live state (thread resolved/unresolved, new review comments, the override label added/removed). Previously succeeded jobs are restored from the CI cache, so the re-run only executes the previously skipped jobs. Review-thread events on PRs from forks carry a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so they are relayed through a trivial `Review Threads Signal` workflow and handled on its `workflow_run` completion in the trusted default-branch context; `PR` workflow completions are watched too, to catch threads resolved while a run was still in flight. A safety cap (5 attempts per run) prevents any reconciliation bug from re-running one workflow forever. - The gate can be bypassed with the new `ignore-unresolved-threads` label (fetched fresh from the API, so adding the label and re-running works; the label also triggers the re-run automatically). `ci-force-all` bypasses it as well, like all other job filtering. - `retry_infra_failures.yml` learned to not treat a `Finish Workflow` failure caused by this merge gate as an infrastructure failure. - Failure direction: if the thread state cannot be fetched at config time, nothing is skipped (fail toward more testing); at finish time the check fails close (the `Mergeable Check` goes red). The `ignore-unresolved-threads` label has been created in the repository. Documentation: a new `Review threads check` section in `docs/resources/develop-contribute/contribute/continuous-integration.mdx`. Tests: `ci/tests/test_review_threads_gate.py` pins the decision functions and their integration into `should_skip_job` (what is skipped, what keeps running, the merge-gate truth table, the commit-status description budget). ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required)

signals.title: CI: run only the selected tests in the sanitizer functional tests in PRs
signals.text: The sanitizer flavors of `Stateless tests` ran the whole suite in every pull request: 17 jobs for the ASan/UBSan, TSan and MSan builds. Under the assumption in the issue - that the stress tests with sanitizers are a stronger check than a plain functional run - those jobs now run only the tests selected for the change. The new `selected tests` option of `ci/jobs/functional_tests.py` runs an ordinary functional test run over the subset that `Targeting` already computes for the targeted check: the tests the pull request changes, the tests that already failed in this pull request, and the tests covering the changed lines according to the coverage database. Unlike the `targeted` check, it does not rerun that selection many times - it is a plain run with a shorter list of tests. The selection is a few hundred tests, so the batches of the full-suite jobs collapse into a single job per flavor: 17 jobs become 8. What still covers the whole suite in a pull request: the debug and plain binary functional test jobs, and the stress tests, which run the functional tests under every sanitizer with heavy concurrency and randomized settings. The master workflow is unchanged and keeps running the full suite in every flavor. Also in this change: * When the selection cannot be fetched (the coverage database or the GitHub diff is unavailable), the job runs the full suite instead of testing less than it would have without the selection, and says so in the report. This also makes a local run of these jobs work. * Tests the job flavor would never run (`no-parallel` tests in a `parallel` job and vice versa) are dropped from the selection, and the job is skipped when nothing is left for it. * `clickhouse-test` exits with code 1 when every test it was given is filtered out - e.g. all the selected tests are tagged `no-tsan` in a TSan job. For a run over an explicit list of tests (flaky, targeted, `selected tests`) that is now reported as SKIPPED instead of a failure; for a full-suite run it stays a failure, since there it means a broken filter. Unit tests for the new logic are in `ci/tests/test_selected_tests_run.py`. `.github/workflows/pull_request.yml` was regenerated via `python3 -m ci.praktika yaml`. ### Verification in this pull request's own CI This pull request changes no source file and no test under `tests/queries`, so nothing is relevant to select and the new jobs correctly report SKIPPED. To exercise the path that actually runs a subset, commit 85362432c858e0cd9aadbf57f2895888b9d35863 temporarily touched `00001_select_1.sql` (reverted in the following commit). On that commit, with all builds served from the cache: * `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, parallel, selected tests)` and `Stateless tests (amd_asan_ubsan, distributed plan, parallel, selected tests)` ran, and the report shows the three selection passes followed by the single selected test - `00001_select_1 OK 1.01s`. * `Stateless tests (amd_asan_ubsan, db disk, distributed plan, sequential, selected tests)` skipped, because the only changed test is parallel-safe and the flavor filter left it nothing to run. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114730&sha=85362432c858e0cd9aadbf57f2895888b9d35863&name_0=PR Possible follow-up, not done here: once the test list is short, the job start dominates the run - in the TSan run above, `Start ClickHouse Server` (which prepares the stateful datasets `test.hits`, `test.visits`, TPC-DS and TPC-H) took 324 seconds out of a 418-second job. Skipping the stateful preparation when no stateful test is selected needs a reliable way to tell, so it is left out of this change. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114725 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ...

signals.title: Keep two refreshable-MV tests runnable on a Replicated database
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112247 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04501_distributed_query_client_version_internal_contexts` and `04661_refreshable_mv_cancel_during_planning` each create a non-APPEND refreshable materialized view over a non-replicated target. On the `DBReplicated` test arm the server refuses that shape by design (`Code: 36 ... refreshable materialized view, no APPEND, replicated database, non-replicated table ... Refusing to create`), so the CREATE always fails and neither test reaches its assertions. This is not intermittent: every run of both tests on that arm carries the refusal, master included. The failures were invisible because the functional-test diagnostics rerun rebuilds the command without the job's own `--replicated-database` flag, so the failure does not reproduce, is labelled flaky, and is reported green on the coverage job. That half is a separate defect, tracked in #112247. I did not add `no-replicated-database`. Both covered sites are APPEND-independent, so an APPEND fixture keeps the tests running on every flavour instead of skipping them, which is what commit `e73f3f142e5f` established for this refusal. Each test switches to `APPEND` with `all_replicas = 1` (`SYSTEM REFRESH VIEW`, `system.processes` and a non-replicated target are all replica-local, so the refresh has to stay on the connected replica), a relative `AFTER 1 YEAR` period, and `EMPTY`. 04661 additionally triggers its one refresh explicitly, which also removes the cross-replica concurrency its old `every 1 second` schedule had. Two test files, no source change. Validated locally against a 3-server Replicated cluster built from `tests/config/install.sh --db-replicated`: both tests fail before the change and pass after it, and reverting each test's covered site (the initiator version fill in `createRefreshContext`; the early `executing_query_status` publication in `refreshTask`) makes the corresponding test fail again, so neither fixture passes vacuously. 100/100 randomized runs green on the Replicated arm and 100/100 on the ordinary one, with no skips.

signals.title: Split 03469_json_read_subcolumns_combined_2_wide_merge_tree into four smaller tests
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `03469_json_read_subcolumns_combined_2_wide_merge_tree` builds an 80k-row Wide-part `JSON` table and runs 71 SELECTs over its subcolumns, 60 of them `format Null` full-table scans. In a Wide part every JSON path/type pair is its own substream, so each scan re-reads all of them, and on object storage under a sanitizer that is a round trip per granule. On `Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, parallel, 1/2)` the worst passing run is 436960 ms against the 600 s cap, on a p50 of 112 s. The compact sibling, same fixture and SELECTs, crossed that cap 6 times in the last 60 days, 4 on master. This is margin restoration, not a fix for a currently red test. @ Avogar asked for this split and scoped it to the public repo. The request was relayed from a repository not readable here, so I have no comment link to give. A `Random settings limits` clamp cannot help here: this test's DDL already pins `index_granularity=8192`, so no randomized value is left to floor. (Such a clamp did fix the compact sibling, whose DDL never pinned it.) The remaining lever is less work per file. This splits the 71 SELECTs across four files, `_2_1_` through `_2_4_`, along the blank-line block seams the file already had. Every statement is carried verbatim and each file repeats the preamble byte for byte, so the four union to the original statement list and their `.reference` files to the original 26 lines. Object storage keeps running all of it: no storage-skip tag and the fixture stays at 80k rows. All four pass with no reference diff, plus 50 randomized runs each. The worst file runs in 43% of the original's wall time on 30% of its scan bytes, still on `Wide` parts with 80000 rows. Arity is four because three was measured and fell short. <details> <summary>Measured per-file cost (local debug build, 3 runs each)</summary> | file | blocks | stmts | wall | vs original | scan MiB | vs original | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | original | 1-11 | 71 | 1.799 s | 100% | 533.2 | 100% | | `_2_1_wide` | 1, 2 | 6 | 0.711 s | 39.5% | 162.6 | 30.5% | | `_2_2_wide` | 3, 4, 5, 6 | 33 | 0.736 s | 40.9% | 144.6 | 27.1% | | `_2_3_wide` | 7, 8 | 14 | 0.699 s | 38.9% | 101.0 | 18.9% | | `_2_4_wide` | 9, 10, 11 | 18 | 0.776 s | 43.2% | 125.1 | 23.5% | A three-file split was implemented and measured first: its worst file was 52.8% of the original's wall time, because block 2 alone is 29% of the scan bytes and blocks are atomic seams. Local disk bounds compute and bytes read, not object-storage latency, so this is a lower bound on the CI win rather than a prediction. The insert preamble now runs four times instead of once, which is the price of the split; at five files the extra preamble costs more than the scan reduction saves. On the clamp: `ClientBase::addMergeTreeSettings` only injects a randomized MergeTree setting when the DDL has not already set it, so `index_granularity=8192` in the `CREATE TABLE` wins. Across the 200 randomized runs, 224 of 224 `CREATE TABLE` statements carried both that pin and `min_rows_for_wide_part=1`, so the granule explosion that hit the compact sibling stays shut in all four copies. `03469_json_read_subcolumns_combined_1_wide_merge_tree` carries a `no-s3-storage, no-azure-blob-storage` "too slow" skip and is arguably a second split candidate, but it is out of scope here. </details>

signals.title: Adaptive lazy execution of short-circuit function arguments (continues #73776)
signals.text: This continues #73776 by @lgbo-ustc, whose branch was ~17 months behind `master` and could no longer be merged mechanically (27 conflicting files in the hottest central code). The author's commits are preserved; on top of them this reconciles the change with the current `master` and reworks the plumbing. Short-circuit evaluation decides *statically* which arguments of `and`, `or`, `if` and `multiIf` are executed lazily. Lazy execution is not free: the rows which are not needed are filtered out and the result is expanded back to the original size. When the filtered out part is small, or the argument itself is cheap, this overhead is larger than the work it saves. This adds an opt-in adaptive mode: the execution of every function is profiled (elapsed time and processed rows), and every 20000 rows the decision is revisited per action - lazy execution is turned off when the estimated cost of the full execution is lower than the measured cost of the lazy execution, and turned back on when the per-row cost of the action grows significantly. Actions whose function can throw an exception on invalid input values (for example `intDiv(1, 0)`) are never switched to eager execution, so the short-circuit protection is preserved. The mode is disabled by default and enabled with the new experimental setting `enable_adaptive_short_circuit_lazy_execution`. Changes on top of the original branch: * The flag no longer travels through `ExpressionStep`/`FilterStep` constructors, the query plan optimizations, the planner and the step serialization. It lives in `ExpressionActionsSettings` next to `enable_lazy_columns_replication`, which removes ~20 files from the change and all the ripple through `QueryPlan/Optimizations`. * `ExpressionActions::execute` and `executeOnColumns` stay `const`; the free `executeAction` became a member with three virtual hooks (`shouldExecuteLazily`, `executeFunction`, `finalizeBlockExecution`) which `AdaptiveExpressionActions` overrides. * The profile plumbing follows the current `IExecutableFunction` chain, including `executeWithoutReplicatedColumns`, which did not exist when the branch was written. * `is_no_except` is computed only when the setting is enabled, so nothing changes for the default path. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Added an experimental setting `enable_adaptive_short_circuit_lazy_execution`, which enables dynamic evaluation of whether a short-circuit function's argument should be lazily executed. The execution of the functions is profiled at runtime, and the lazy execution of an argument is disabled when it costs more than executing the argument on all the rows. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73776

signals.title: Build Debian packages for the release builds only
signals.text: The `Stress test` was the only job installing the Debian packages of the debug, sanitizer and CFI builds, and it can take the plain `clickhouse` binary instead — that binary is built and uploaded for every build type anyway. Every other consumer of the packages (`Install packages`, `Compatibility check`, `Upgrade check`, the server Docker images and the release jobs) runs on a release build. So the release builds keep their packages, and nine of the eleven packaging steps go away, together with the `DESTDIR` install that copies the whole binary, and the upload and download of the resulting packages. The stress test now sets up the paths the packages own from the binary: `install_binary` in `stress_tests.lib` symlinks `/usr/bin/clickhouse*` at it, installs the default `config.xml` and `users.xml`, and unpacks the self-extracting archive up front — decompressing a sanitizer build under `clickhouse start` would eat into its wait for the pid file and race any concurrent `clickhouse local`. `install_packages` stays for the upgrade check, which installs an actual release. Symbolization is unaffected: `clickhouse_split_debug_symbols` leaves `programs/clickhouse` untouched and strips only the copy it installs, so the binary artifact carries its debug info even for a release build. For the sanitizer builds `clickhouse-common-static-dbg` was empty to begin with, since they do not set `SPLIT_DEBUG_SYMBOLS`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required)

signals.title: Fix a server crash when merging -OrNull/-OrDefault states under group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114690 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a server crash that happens when aggregate states of the `-OrNull` or `-OrDefault` combinators are merged with `group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'` and a non-zero `max_rows_to_group_by`, for example when a query reads through an aggregate projection. ### Description Under `group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'` the aggregator freezes its hash table once `max_rows_to_group_by` is exceeded, and every subsequent row whose key is absent gets the overflow-row pointer. That pointer is `nullptr` whenever `overflow_row` is off, which is the case for any query that is not `GROUP BY ... WITH TOTALS`, so `places[i] == nullptr` is a normal value on the merge path meaning "this key did not fit, skip the row". `Aggregator::mergeStreamsImplCase` states this in an in-source comment and hands the array to `mergeBatch` without filtering. Every batch consumer honours that contract except `AggregateFunctionOrFill::mergeBatch`, which unconditionally dereferenced `places[i]` to OR its trailing "was anything aggregated" flag byte, so a null place became a write through a null pointer. `IAggregateFunctionHelper::mergeBatch` and `AggregateFunctionOrFill::addBatch` already carry the same `if (places[i])` guard; this adds the third and last instance of it. Reproduced on master `bf580ecb357f39df87f814ad214698f2c8aeab17` with a debug build: a `MergeTree` table with an aggregate projection queried with `max_rows_to_group_by = 10, group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'` dies with `Address: 0x8. Access: write` at `AggregateFunctionOrFill.h:258`, for both `-OrNull` and `-OrDefault` and for both the single-number and the fixed-keys aggregation methods. The added test covers those arms plus both `-Tuple`/`-OrNull` nesting orders, and fails (the server dies) without the change. Behaviour changes only for rows the aggregator has already decided to drop, so no query that never trips `max_rows_to_group_by` under mode `any` is affected. Found by the targeted AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)` and `..., old_compatibility`, STID 2575-398a): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114690&sha=9b5110134d760b3aace6e8c767073cb51c338233&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29. The defect is on master and independent of that PR, which only made the path easier to hit.

signals.title: Fix logical error when FINAL column pruning would grow the read header
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/91849 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Unexpected number of kept output positions after removing unused columns from `ReadFromMergeTree`") raised by a `SELECT ... FINAL` whose `PREWHERE` uses a column that `FINAL` needs for merging (`ver`, `is_deleted`, `sign`) and which does not project that column. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/91849 ### Description A `SELECT ... FINAL` whose `PREWHERE` consumes a column that `FINAL` needs for merging, and which does not project that column, fails with `LOGICAL_ERROR: Unexpected number of kept output positions after removing unused columns from ReadFromMergeTree: expected 3, got 2`. Root cause: `ReadFromMergeTree::removeUnusedColumns` computes the caller's vector of output positions once, so it holds as many entries as the output header had *before* pruning. Pruning then re-adds any `FINAL`-required or `PREWHERE`-input column that `PREWHERE` had erased from that header, making the recomputed header longer than the vector. The assertion is correct and stays: `kept_output_positions` is consumed positionally, so a short vector would pair columns with the wrong inputs and return wrong results rather than fail. The correct positions cannot be recovered afterwards, because `ActionsDAG::updateHeader` matches inputs by name and reorders them. So the request is refused instead: `canRemoveUnusedColumns()` now returns `false` when a `FINAL`-required column is read but absent from the output header, the necessary condition for the header to grow. One check gates every caller, and the read plan is left intact. The guard is narrow rather than a blanket bail-out for `FINAL`: instrumenting the predicate against the real outcome of every `removeUnusedColumns` call over 61 in-tree `FINAL`/`PREWHERE` tests recorded 26 prunings, all with the predicate false, and none where it was true and a pruning would have happened. Found by the AST fuzzer and the stress test on unrelated pull requests. Both fuzzed queries read through `merge()`, but it is not required: the failure reproduces on a plain `FROM t FINAL`. - `AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107305&sha=1a49e7372d0f969cd06d7ba237d8eb3b3461e814&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 - `Stress test (arm_asan_ubsan, s3)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108069&sha=77f495e71c33bb2c27441fa12f9deb0fdb7e24f2&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29 <details> <summary>Coverage across merging modes and sibling implementations</summary> The regression test covers one arm per merging mode, since the set of columns `FINAL` requires (and therefore the size of the mismatch) differs per mode. Every arm fails without the change: | arm | mismatch | |---|---| | `ReplacingMergeTree(ver, is_deleted)`, top-level | expected 4, got 2 | | `ReplacingMergeTree(ver, is_deleted)`, via `merge()` | expected 4, got 2 | | `ReplacingMergeTree(ver)` | expected 3, got 2 | | `CollapsingMergeTree(sign)` | expected 3, got 2 | | `VersionedCollapsingMergeTree(sign, ver)` | expected 4, got 2 | `Graphite` is already excluded from this optimization on the preceding lines. The predicate never reads `merging_params` directly, only the name set `getColumnsRequiredForMergingFinal` returns, so one check handles every mode. Other implementations of `removeUnusedColumns` need no equivalent guard: `FilterStep` and `ExpressionStep` cannot return more positions than they were asked for, `JoinStepLogical` legitimately grows its header and declares that separately, and the `IQueryPlanStep` default reports no change. `ReplicatedMergeTree` and `SharedMergeTree` read through `ReadFromMergeTree`, so there is no second read step to mirror the check into. `04224_special_columns_prewhere_final_91849`, the regression test for #91849 that added the widening this change must not remove, stays green. </details>

signals.title: Remove `WINDOW VIEW`
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/61069 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/88706 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `WINDOW VIEW` feature is removed, together with the `WATCH` statement and the `windowID` function. It has been non-functional since version 24.12 (inserts into the source table were silently not delivered to window views) and was never supported by the analyzer, which is enabled by default since 24.3. The settings `allow_experimental_window_view`, `window_view_clean_interval`, `window_view_heartbeat_interval`, and `wait_for_window_view_fire_signal_timeout` are kept as obsolete no-ops. The time-window functions `tumble`, `tumbleStart`, `tumbleEnd`, `hop`, `hopStart`, and `hopEnd` are kept. If you still have window views defined, drop them before upgrading, since a server with a window view left in its metadata will fail to load it. Similar functionality will be reimplemented on top of streaming queries (issue [#114738](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738)). The removal, in detail: - `src/Storages/WindowView/` (`StorageWindowView`, `WindowViewSource`, `StorageBlocks`), `WatermarkTransform`, the `ParserCreateWindowViewQuery` parser, and the whole `WATCH` statement stack (`ParserWatchQuery`, `ASTWatchQuery`, `InterpreterWatchQuery`, the `IStorage::watch` virtual) — window views were the last implementor of `watch`, and the `WATCH` statement was already documented as deprecated. - The `ASTCreateQuery` watermark/lateness fields and their AST JSON serialization and validation; the `PushingToWindowViewSink` and `ViewType::WINDOW` branches in `InsertDependenciesBuilder`; window-view special cases in `InterpreterCreateQuery`, `InterpreterInsertQuery`, `StorageFactory`, `DatabaseOrdinary`, `DatabaseReplicated`, `DDLDependencyVisitor`, `QueryFuzzer`, BuzzHouse, and the ArrowFlight table-type mapping. - The `windowID` function and the `UInt32` single-argument forms of `tumbleStart`/`tumbleEnd`/`hopStart`/`hopEnd` (they only accepted `windowID` output). The rest of the time-window function family stays, since these are ordinary functions usable in a regular `GROUP BY` and are exactly the vocabulary for the streaming-queries replacement. - The keywords `WATCH`, `EVENTS`, `ALLOWED_LATENESS`, and `STRICTLY_ASCENDING` (the `WATERMARK` keyword stays: the streaming-queries `WATERMARK FOR` clause uses it), the error code `QUERY_IS_NOT_SUPPORTED_IN_WINDOW_VIEW`, and the corresponding fuzzer dictionary and ANTLR grammar entries. - Kept for compatibility: `QueryViewsLogElement::ViewType::WINDOW` (so existing `system.query_views_log` tables keep their schema) and `ViewTarget::Inner` (so old DDL log entries still parse), following the same pattern as the `LIVE VIEW` removal. - Tests: the four remaining window-view tests are removed. The pure time-window-function coverage of `01049_window_view_window_functions` moved to a new `04891_time_window_functions` test, which also pins the new `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` behavior of `tumbleStart(UInt32)`. - Docs: the `Window View` section of `CREATE VIEW`, the `WATCH` page (with its navigation entries and locale twins) are removed and the old-slug redirects retargeted; the window-view entries are removed from the generated settings/functions reference pages (second commit, hence the `pr-autogenerated-docs` label): the `window-view.mdx` settings page, the four settings' entries in the pages/manifest/navigation/settings explorer, and the `windowID` section of `time-window-functions.mdx`. The unrelated drift accumulated on master since the last nightly regeneration is deliberately not included; the nightly docs-autogen job will pick it up. Why now: the feature has been non-functional since Dec 2024 — commit `ceae84c87a2` removed the explicit view-dependency registration and `DDLDependencyVisitor` never extracted the source table of a `CREATE WINDOW VIEW`, so inserts into the source table were silently not pushed to window views, and direct inserts failed with `std::out_of_range` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493). Nobody noticed for ~1.5 years. It was never ported to the analyzer (with `enable_analyzer = 1`, the default, existing window views load permanently inert), its tests were removed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73822 because they were inherently flaky, and it kept costing triage time (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 is a recent server SIGSEGV through `getSourceTableSelectQuery`). The full assessment, including the plan for reimplementing this functionality on top of streaming queries (`SELECT ... FROM t STREAM`, `WATERMARK FOR`, emit-on-watermark windowed aggregation), is in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Treat a NULL nullable string column on the right of IN as absent
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN` for a tuple on the left of `IN` and a `Nullable(String)` column on the right, as in `SELECT (1, 2) IN (rhs) FROM (SELECT CAST(NULL AS Nullable(String)) AS rhs)`. A `NULL` value of such a column is now an absent set element, so the query returns `0` for `IN` and `1` for `NOT IN`, matching the constant right-hand side and the `Nullable(Nothing)` column already covered by test `04870`. ### Description Follow-up to #104993 for the review finding at https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993#discussion_r3773210901. The row-wise rewrite for a bare column on the right of `IN` casts a string-typed right-hand side to the tuple type of the left-hand side. Its guard strips `Nullable` and `LowCardinality`, so a `Nullable(String)` column enters that branch, while the cast target stays the non-`Nullable` tuple. `CAST(Nullable(String) -> Tuple(...))` rejects a `NULL` source value, so the `NULL` row failed with `Code: 349 CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN` instead of being treated as absent from the set. The fix handles nullability before the cast and keeps the cast target non-`Nullable`, as the block intends: * the right-hand side is wrapped in `ifNull(rhs, <tuple default>)`, which makes the cast total, so it cannot throw whatever `short_circuit_function_evaluation` is set to; * the comparison is wrapped in `if(isNull(rhs), <absent>, ...)`, which supplies the "element absent" answer and makes the substituted value unreachable. Both layers are needed: without the guard, a left-hand tuple that equals the substituted default compares equal and returns wrong results; without the substitution, a lazy guard alone still throws under `short_circuit_function_evaluation = 'disable'`. Test `04898` pins each direction, and its left-hand tuples are the default value of their type on purpose so that removing the guard reddens it. Only the `NULL` row changes. A present value is still parsed and compared, a non-parseable one still raises `CANNOT_PARSE_INPUT_ASSERTION_FAILED` (`04871`), a plain `String` right-hand side keeps its exact node shape, a `Nullable` tuple on the left keeps its three-valued result, and a tuple with a bare `Nothing` element keeps the previous lowering because it has no default value to substitute. `FixedString` is excluded because its cast to a tuple is unsupported for either nullability.
